description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Operating Systems topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: operating-systems

facts.claim: An OS manages hardware and software resources and provides services

source.quote: system software that manages computer hardware and software resources, and provides common services for computer programs

facts.claim: It is an intermediary between programs and hardware

source.quote: the operating system acts as an intermediary between programs and the computer hardware

facts.claim: Running, ready and waiting/blocked states

source.quote: changes the state to "running" while the previously "running" process is stored in a "waiting" state

facts.claim: A process waiting for I/O is blocked

source.quote: If a process requests something for which it must wait, it will be blocked

facts.claim: Save the running process's state and load the next one's

source.quote: the operating system must save the state of the currently running process, followed by loading the next process state

facts.claim: A thread is the smallest unit the scheduler manages

source.quote: a thread of execution is the smallest sequence of programmed instructions that can be managed independently by a scheduler

facts.claim: Threads of a process share its memory and resources

source.quote: sharing resources such as memory, while different processes do not share these resources

facts.claim: Each process gets a time slice (quantum) in circular order

source.quote: time slices (also known as time quanta) are assigned to each process in equal portions and in circular order

facts.claim: Round robin is starvation-free

source.quote: Round-robin scheduling is simple, easy to implement, and starvation-free

facts.claim: A critical section needs mutual exclusion

source.quote: A critical section is a piece of a program that requires mutual exclusion of access

facts.claim: It is where shared resources are accessed

source.quote: the parts of the program where the shared resource is accessed need to be protected

facts.claim: A semaphore controls access to a shared resource by many processes

source.quote: a semaphore is a synchronization device used to control access to a common resource by multiple threads or processes

facts.claim: It records how many units of a resource are available

source.quote: a record of how many units of a particular resource are available

facts.claim: Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait

source.quote: Hold and wait or resource holding: a process is currently holding at least one resource and requesting additional resources

facts.claim: Circular wait

source.quote: Circular wait: each process must be waiting for a resource which is being held by another process

facts.claim: Banker's algorithm avoids deadlock by keeping the system in a safe state

source.quote: the bank never leaves a safe state

facts.claim: Each process declares its maximum need in advance

source.quote: it must declare the maximum number of instances of each resource type that it may ever claim

facts.claim: Memory is split into fixed-size pages and frames

source.quote: the operating system retrieves data from secondary storage in blocks of the same size (pages)

facts.claim: A page table maps pages to frames

source.quote: use either a set of page address registers or in-memory page tables

facts.claim: A page fault happens when the page is not in memory

source.quote: Page replacement happens when a requested page is not in memory (page fault)

facts.claim: LRU and FIFO are common replacement policies

source.quote: LRU (least recently used) approximations

facts.claim: Virtual addresses are mapped to physical addresses

source.quote: maps memory addresses used by a program, called virtual addresses, into physical addresses in computer memory

facts.claim: Disk extends memory beyond the size of RAM

source.quote: utilizing, e.g., disk storage, to provide a virtual address space that can exceed the capacity of real memory
